utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, case number IT-95-16-T, The Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. To answer the question that you asked yesterday, I should like to indicate that the request of Mrs. Slokovic-Glumac to have the Judge from Zenica heard as a Court witness, we have no objection. However, there are two other problems which require an urgent decision of the Court, but for this I would need 10 to 15 minutes, and perhaps you would find a more appropriate time to do this. Perhaps we should finish with the witness first. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I think Counsel Radovic was examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't want to say anything in particular, but I am continuing with the examination of the witness, and it's up to you to decide whether we will follow the proposal by Mr. Terrier or we will continue with the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No. My intention was to continue with the examination of this witness as Mr. Terrier suggested. After that only could we come to that particular matter he would like to raise. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Would the witness be shown document P335?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you something about this document and then you will pay attention to the parts that I will indicate. Please look at the title first. Who is the document addressed to? It's in the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Travnik defence administration to the Vitez defence office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how these defence administrations were organised? Was this administration above the Vitez defence office?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: And who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The document was signed by head of the defence office, Mr. Marijan Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: And he was a representative of the defence office of the HVO government in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Now, since the document is entitled "Report," and I'm not sure that the document in English sounds the same as it does in Croatian, I would like to ask for your interpretation of some of the things from this document. Look at item 3 under "Notes," the first sentence says, "The formation of the Viteska Brigade did not progress according to the anticipated timetable." How do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Since -- it probably had difficulties. There was the problem of mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: All right. Then it says -- underneath the note it says, under the second 3, "In the period of 16th of April, up to and including April 28th, 1993, a total of 498 conscripts were mobilised." Could you please tell us whether you can conclude from this sentence on which date was the individual mobilisation carried out?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, of course you cannot conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: So how do you interpret the following? So the item underneath that it says, "Military conscripts were mobilised, which were used as replacements on the lines after the first assault, i.e. they are gradually included as replacements for the soldiers from the mobile personnel." How do you understand this? Who participated in the first assault?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, this is what it says here, that mobile personnel participated in the first assault and then immediately after that other conscripts were mobilised. In other words, in the period from the 16th of April until the 28th of April, a total of 498 additional conscripts were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who is considered to be part of the mobile personnel as it says here?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I spoke a little bit about that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Just tell us briefly.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are considered to be people who had certain contracts signed with the defence office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: So let's go to the list of these names which are attached to this document. Have you found that? There is a whole list of names. Please look at this list of names, look it at carefully, and in markings can you tell from this list, from any of the persons, can it be concluded in which period between the 16th and the 28th of April where they mobilised? Please look at it carefully, think about it and then reply. Just these above the line.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: From this list you cannot tell when each of these persons was mobilised. I don't see that anywhere. So it can be concluded that these people, in this period that is cited, this period of 12 days, were sent to some of the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: But when they were deployed, you can't see that?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, you can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Radovic. Counsel Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Alilovic. If I understood you yesterday in the course of your examination, you mentioned attempts by the BH army to cut some important road communications before the conflict and in the course of the conflict. My question is: What is your information about which places and which towns did the army of B and H try to cut off or to prevent communications in the Lasva Valley and broader in Central Bosnia, if you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I spoke about this yesterday. The conflict in Busovaca, in January, the first thing that happened was that communications were cut and Busovaca and Kiseljak were separated in the length of about 10 to 13 kilometres. During the conflict in Vitez, they tried to do that in Vitez as well, and I said that the barricades from the 20th of October was an attempt to separate the forces between Vitez and Busovaca, or to cut Vitez practically in two, and this way to divide, to separate Vitez and Busovaca. This was attempted throughout the conflict by the B and H army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the fact that the HVO government was considering for a while to evacuate the population during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know about this. We were preparing to cut through a new road for possible evacuation of the population if it was -- if it became impossible to resist the attack, so then there was a complete blockade, so it wasn't possible to carry this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, would the HVO successfully -- would it be able to successfully resist the B and H army in view of the equipment and the force of the army? What was the situation in Central Bosnia, and could you tell us what the situation was in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said a little bit about this yesterday, and I personally think and the figures speak for themselves. I think that this was impossible, and what happened in Vitez in such a small area, struggling for our bare lives and surviving for as long as we did, I can hardly explain that myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: According to your information, when did the Muslims start seriously preparing for the conflict? Did they -- perhaps were the events from Slimena have any influence on these events?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely, even after they received arms, considerable quantities of arms. And for a long time after that we could not agree to go where we had the common need, where there was our common need to go. After that, a few months after that, the B and H army, i.e. the Muslims, started to behave differently. They didn't ever want, and I couldn't explain this, to use our joint forces where this was needed, and attempts to do this over a long period of time were not successful. This barricade -- all of these barricades and the incidents and events that happened point to the fact that even after that we did -- we did not take the steps together that we should have taken, and it happened -- things happened that did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information about when the defence department in Vitez started to mobilise people? Was this after the armed incident?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I came to work, to the post office where I was staying, for the third day -- after the third day for the first time, and then I would get there regularly every day. I would spend time in my office. I could see, because the defence department was close by, I could see that it was preparing seriously for mobilisation, and the serious mobilisation efforts began only then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday that in Buhine Kuce, about 35 people were killed?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when this happened, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: This happened at the beginning of '93 -- I'm sorry, '94, shortly after New Year. I think that's when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the units of the B and H army were located in Buhine Kuce?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This was the line of separation. That's what I know. So my answer is affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the end of the conflict -- at the beginning of the conflict, the communication between Vitez and Busovaca was cut for a while at Buhine Kuce because of gunfire from positions of the B and H army, so that traffic along that road was impossible and it was redirected to Radak bridge and along the Lasva River? Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is how it was during the whole of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know if he had participated in the making of some political or military decisions at the time of the conflict, before the conflict, particularly relating to this time period that we're concerned with?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as taking part in the planning, I believe that he didn't participate in that because he wasn't holding a post from which he could participate in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Puliselic. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Alilovic. I would like to show you some documents and ask you some questions in order to make corrections to the transcript because there were some things that were not entered properly into the transcript. This is relating to Buhine Kuce; there were 35 victims. And you also mentioned Krizancevo Selo. How many casualties were there?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think 65 or 66 people were killed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Also you said that in the second half of '92, Merhamet was founded.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, in the second half of '92.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was the parish office of Caritas continuing to supply the Muslims with humanitarian aid; is that so?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but in smaller quantities than before. I said this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did this continue in the course of '93?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it did not because this simply was not possible except for parts which were under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: This is what I'm asking about, which were under the control of the HVO. So you could take supplies to Mahala?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. This continued and even more intensely than before, because during the war, I took over the coordination of the humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So the citizens, Muslims, who happened to be on the territory under the control of the HVO continued to receive assistance from Caritas?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely, because we, in fact, distributed all the food that we got from the humanitarian aid through Caritas because it had the staff and it was able to do this, it had the necessary transportation, so we maintained this system of supply throughout the war. Also, there was the Red Cross which had certain quantities and for certain categories; it also supplied the citizens. There was another humanitarian organisation, Mother and Child, which was established during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know who was responsible for the technical aspect of aid distribution at Caritas? Who was working at Caritas?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zeljko Blaz was working at Caritas. He had a small group of people who were in charge of these matters, and I coordinated this, as I said, from the beginning of the war onwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at a document now? Could you tell us whether you remember ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D48/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this is an HVO document signed by the president of the HVO government. Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the stamp?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So president of the HVO, Ivan Santic. Do you remember this situation where aid was requested for 160 of the most imperilled families in the villages of Preocica and Lupac?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I wonder why you don't have more of these documents. The situation in certain villages was always more difficult. These were in the bordering villages towards Lasva or towards Zenica where there was a vast number of refugees as well, and the social conditions at that time were more difficult than in Vitez itself, and Mr. Santic, I think on several occasions in this way, while the UNHCR was still present in Vitez and it was present there, at the end of October it left Vitez, but some members of staff remained there. He, on several occasions, made these attempts to try to resolve the most serious situations in the municipality of Vitez. This was one of his characteristics.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the ethnic make-up of the population in the village of Preocica was, for whom the aid was requested?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The ethnic make-up of Lupac and Preocica was about 98 or 99 per cent Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any Croats in Lupac?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, even though in Preocica we had a sales outlet, and we tried to do that in Lupac as well, but I don't know if there were any Croats in those villages. Maybe the occasional Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So these were exclusively Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they were exclusively Muslim villages, for the most part Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I will show you another document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D49/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, do you recognise the stamp and the signature of Mr. Ivan Santic here?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you remember this decision?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember this decision, but the person who is receiving this assistance, I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this is a decision by the HVO government of the 9th of December of '92 to give assistance to Mr. Adem Beslic for eyesight surgery. Tell us, is Mr. Adem Beslic a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to his name and last name, he is a Muslim, but I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were there other such decisions to help the most needy, the neediest people in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were such decisions, and Caritas helped us a lot in such cases, and I spoke about that yesterday and a little bit earlier this morning, so this is how we would solve such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What was the average salary in Vitez at that time, in December of '92?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The average salary in July or August, when I was taking the data for the local municipal accounting office, at the factory of industrial explosives, for example, the salary was 38 German marks per month. In December, it probably didn't even come to 20 German marks, but I don't remember exactly. So this would be the figure after the periodic calculation for '92, so 38 German marks. At the level of the municipality, the salary was much lower. My salary, for example, was 60 German marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The period we are talking about, December and the beginning of 1993, January?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: By then, I think that very few people were actually working, so that the average salary must have been much lower than the one I mentioned for August, which means much below 38 German marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Therefore, this was a substantial sum in those days?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Indeed. It amounted to 10 or 12 average salaries and probably even more.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I will now ask you to look at some permits issued by the HVO for trade and transport of goods, so please look at this permit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D50/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this is a permit for the movement of persons and goods?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It is a customary document in form that used to be issued in those days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It was signed by the president of the HVO municipality of Vitez, Ivica Santic. You recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You also see the signature of Tihomir Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I see it on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So tell us, please, what is actually permitted by this document?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: This document gives permission, in the first place, for the movement of vehicles up to a part of the special purpose industry and the transport of certain goods -- equipment, rather, and weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So transportation is permitted --

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: -- of these shell cases, 120-millimetre mortars, and three delivery forms.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The goods come from the SPS Vitez, that is a factory, the section producing special purpose equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was there a BH army logistics centre in Visoko?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there may have been one, but for the BH army forces because that was in a Muslim area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the presence of the BH army in Visoko?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned yesterday that until the outbreak of the conflict, as far as I know, all equipment of this kind was shared with the BH army in Vitez, and as far as I know, deliveries did not cease until the outbreak of the conflict, deliveries of this kind of equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this permit for the movement and trade of goods was signed by the president of the municipality, does it mean that, in a sense, he was a participant in the agreement reached between the BH army and the HVO as regards the transportation of ammunition, as we can see from this document?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether he often participated in the talks, but this was the normal format of permits of this kind for allowing passage of goods of any kind, including this kind of goods, so that he was involved in these matters related to the transportation of goods.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So all types of permits of this kind were issued by the HVO municipality?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When it came to the transportation of military materiel, then clearly the HVO military had to participate or, rather, its representatives?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you see such documents before relating to military materiel?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have seen this kind of permit but not the actual delivery forms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have another document to show the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D51/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, have you read this document? Do you recall this extraordinary session held on the 24th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were you present?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was. I was present.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: This announcement of the civilian authorities actually is a reaction to the events that occurred immediately prior to this, that is, the beginning of the conflict until the 24th of April?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Under item 3, it is stated that the Command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia is requested to carry out a detailed investigation of all individual cases of flagrant violation of international humanitarian law. And then it goes on to say that a particularly detailed and efficient investigation is required for cases of killed civilians, destruction and torching of civilian facilities in all conflicts to date. Tell us, please, what kind of a request was this? Did the HVO government have any jurisdiction over the command of the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: It felt the need to do this, and that is why it did so, to let the command know, because we had some more detailed knowledge about what was happening on the ground, and it was with that aim in mind that this request actually was made to units as to the way they should behave and what they should do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were asking the command of the Operative Zone to act, does that mean that you thought that the perpetrators of those acts could have been soldiers because otherwise you had your own civilian police?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, we had a civilian police, but it was also a part of the units, in a sense, and this was actually a request to the HVO forces as to the way they should behave and what they should do. That is at least how I understood it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you thought that it was necessary to establish who was responsible for any violations of international humanitarian law?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you were prompted to take such action because you had heard of a number of cases?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately by this date at this session and others that preceded it, I heard about all these events and what took place until then, and, of course, afterwards as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was the number of victims in Ahmici known by this date, the 24th of April?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe so, but I don't recall exactly now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Also under item 2, it is stated that the HVO government of Vitez unanimously condemns all recorded crimes committed during conflict between the BH army and the HVO by any party.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That was the position of the government; wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that was the position of the government, because probably already by then the casualty figures were known. Also, we had some information about the crimes committed, at least I was informed about them at that meeting, and as an individual and as a member of the government, I fully supported such a position.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Under point 4 too, another request is made to the HVO command and the BH army command to exchange innocent detained civilians as soon as possible. That request was also one of the important conclusions reached at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The meeting adopted the conclusion, as far as I can remember, to try and come to an agreement as soon as possible with the Muslim side over the exchange of detainees, and through the UNPROFOR, I think a meeting was arranged, and in the days that followed an agreement was, in fact, reached on exchange, and in those negotiations Pero Skopljak participated as the vice-president, or, rather, the person who was assigned to take change of matters related to exchange.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the exchange was actually carried out?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, the agreement -- I can't remember -- I don't know exactly when the meeting was held in the UNPROFOR base, but I do know there was one around that time, and that Mr. Skopljak participated as well as the brigade commander -- whether anyone else participated I don't know, I don't remember -- and that an exchange of the detainees in Vitez for some people -- some Croats from the territory of Zenica. Therefore, an exchange of Muslims from Vitez for Croats from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was the exchange carried out?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know from these meetings Muslims were given to Zenica, but as far as I know, hardly any Croats came from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You actually said that Muslim detainees were released by the Croats, whereas the BH army did not release Croats. Is that what you said? Croats detained in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did the HVO government frequently issue announcements and requests of this kind addressed to the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it would issue similar such documents, but I think this wasn't frequent, because Mr. Santic was in contact, almost on a daily basis, with them, as well as Pero Skopljak as the person in charge of the exchange, as I said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let me show you another document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D52/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature on this document of Ivan Santic?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I'm also familiar with the contents of this letter, and I myself talked to Mr. Santic about this and he asked me about my opinion. Of course, I was fully in agreement with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this is a document whereby the HVO government is proposing the release of a part of the detained Muslims to the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. So this letter and this request was something that happened outside the negotiations between the HVO and the BH army?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Actually, I thought that this happened before the meeting, when the first steps were agreed as to negotiations over an exchange in the UNPROFOR base. Why this document bears this date, I really don't know, because I think that actually it happened earlier, and I think that a part of this recommendation was, in fact, implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you mean that a part of the people were released prior to the formal agreement on the exchange?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I was able to hear from Mr. Santic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many people were involved?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not. I know, for instance, that Mr. Mujezinovic was there for a time, some professors, that some of them were released, but I really don't know exactly whom or how many of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have one further question linked to your testimony. You said that your main job was procurement of food and supply of the population; wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When purchasing food, did you bear in mind the different foodstuffs used by various ethnic groups? For example, the fat that is used by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It is well-known that Muslims do not consume lard, and oil was always an item -- or rather vegetable oil, vegetable fat. But also a large number of Croats consume oil rather than lard, so that the range of goods offered was quite satisfactory if that is what you had in mind, that perhaps we didn't procure enough food stuffs that Muslims consume.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that the -- this process of supply continued in October. Did it continue after the Muslims returned to Ahmici, after the roadblock was removed?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Supplies continued for as long as it was possible to move around at all, and already in October we had considerable quantities in stock so that citizens were still able to purchase goods in the shops. Yesterday, I think, we reviewed a document, a permit by Mr. Kupreskic, issued after the removal of that roadblock, even though by then movement was more difficult than prior to that event but movement did occur.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you remember for how long this method of supply with packages continued, with food parcels?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it went on until October or November. Actually, until all demands by citizens had been met, demands for this kind of food.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell us once more, for the record, what was the name of the person working in Caritas with the distribution of aid?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The person in charge of Caritas, I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Just give us the name.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Was Mr. Zeljko Blaz and he is still performing that same role today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions for this witness. I should just like to tender into evidence the documents from the exhibits. Could you help me, Mr. Bos, with the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: D48 to D52/2, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. No objection, so they are admitted into evidence. Before we move on to the Prosecution, I would like to clarify the way we intend to apply the provisional ruling we made yesterday. Let us now consider the particular case of the present witness, Mr. Alilovic. Now, I see from my documents that he has been called by three Defence counsel, Susak, Radovic and Slokovic-Glumac. So as a witness for the three defendants who -- on behalf of whom the Defence counsel I've just mentioned are acting here. Now, that means that after the cross-examination by the Prosecution, only those three these Defence counsel will be allowed to re-examine the witness. The other counsel, namely Counsel Par, Pavkovic and Puliselic, have cross-examined the witness after the examination-in-chief. Is it clear? Mrs. Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, in view of the fact that I was the author of this list, may I clarify it? This list was done on the basis of counts. With respect to Count 1, we have listed witnesses who will be testifying to the joint circumstances of the indictment, and they are actually joint witnesses for all the accused. So as to avoid any misunderstanding, under Count 1, all the witnesses are joint witnesses. It was only a question of my writing the list. But this witness, for instance, was called by colleague Susak. As for the facts they are testifying to, they are common to all, and these other counsel did not separately indicate their witnesses for Count 1, they're all on this same list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. However, it is a fact that when we were given the lists of witnesses for each defendant, Mr. Alilovic was only mentioned in the list of witnesses drafted by and filed by Counsel Susak, by yourself and Counsel Radovic. Subsequently you provided us a list of all defendants' list of witnesses except Vlatko Kupreskic. You are referring to that particular document. Here no mention is made of --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: -- of the fact that all those -- about 20 -- actually, 41 witnesses, witnesses for the six defendants. No mention is made there. You may, of course, be aware that if we start having the examination-in-chief of 41 witnesses by six Defence counsel, then cross-examination and then re-examination-in-chief, we will end probably this trial in two years time. So we must come to some sort of -- I would like to stick to what you had proposed initially, each of you had proposed initially in the lists of witnesses you filed with the Tribunal, and each Defence counsel set out on paper a list of a certain number of witnesses. If those witnesses coincide, that means that the particular witness may be examined-in-chief by more than one Defence counsel. Otherwise, he will be examined-in-chief only by one. Otherwise, it's a sort of Pandora's box. So I insist, at least for Mr. Alilovic, since it is very clear from the lists filed by Counsel Susak, Counsel Radovic and Counsel Slokovic-Glumac that only they intended to call Mr. Alilovic as a witness, they will only be entitled to re-examination after the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I wonder whether the Prosecution is now prepared to cross-examine the witness. What about the procedural matters Mr. Terrier intended to raise? Are they linked to this particular issue or could we take them up the later on if there is no link to this question which -- no. So later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning. With your leave, I will be cross-examining this witness, Mr. Alilovic. Good morning Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Alilovic. Mr. Alilovic, you stated in your evidence that relations began to deteriorate between the Croat and Muslim populations in Vitez municipality because, in essence, the Croats felt that the Muslims were unsupportive against the threat, as you say, of Serb aggression. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And, in fact, you felt that the Muslims should be taking active steps to support you in what was then a war, to use that term, between Croatia and the Serbs; is that so?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: As time went on, particularly into 1992, you say that the Muslims had very much opposing views about the Serb threat and, at one point, even decreed neutrality, not to have a part in that war?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, neutrality was declared at the beginning of '92, I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I believe I am right in saying that you also said that it was at around that time the Croat population of the area felt it was necessary to prepare to defend themselves?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And, again, that this was still directed towards the threat of, as you saw it, Serb aggression?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that one initiative taken was, of course, forming the HVO; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And the term "HVO" covers essentially two items, does it not: one, a civilian government, and the other, a military regime?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: A military component, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Under whatever constitution was drawn for the HVO, is it true that the military component would have the major power in the event of threat or imminent threat of war or conflict?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't feel this to be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, were you aware of any form of decree or ordinance to that end or not?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You have stated that your role before and during the conflict that followed remained in the economic sphere, in food supply and the like; that is correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So just to clear one small point. When invited by Defence counsel to comment on military strategy or other matters, you do so from just a degree of general knowledge, not from any military knowledge as such?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you say that one initiative taken by the HVO was to seize quantities of weapons.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I presume it was the military component that carried out that operation?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the military component did undertake the operation, but this operation was also discussed by the civilian authorities, and they supported this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And it --

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was recommended -- I apologise -- recommended and supported.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you say that as a result of that, there was the proposal that there should be equal sharing of the weapons?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This was a request by the Muslim side, so an agreement was reached in this sense, as I said, for the weapons to be shared; and as far as I know, this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I would ask you, sir: Do you have any direct knowledge that it was done?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I had the opportunity to hear this on several occasions at official public meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But you did not have any personal administrative hand in the transfer of weapons between people, or supply of weapons?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Forgive me, but it seems a little illogical to divide up weaponry in that fashion between a force that is trying to prepare for its defence and one that you described as inert and not wish you to take part in the war?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't mean it that way, if we understood one another well. Up until then, there were relatively few weapons, and the HVO launched an initiative to acquire weapons due to the overall military and political circumstances at that time, and you could hear this in the media based on the assumption that the Serbian side was trying to link its forces from Vlasic to Kobiljaca, and it was necessary to urgently obtain as much weaponry as possible in order to resist. In order to organise a resistance, it was important to mobilise all forces, both Croat and Muslim. So the intention during that whole time was to move in that direction to ensure joint efforts towards a unified approach, unified resistance, towards our common enemy. So in that sense, when I said that, this is what I meant the entire time until, unfortunately, that incident occurred, and that is our greatest tragedy, because we could not find a common solution. So this is what I was talking about, and I hope that we understood one another well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Alilovic, that Mr. Dario Kordic actually issued an order that the agreement over the Busovaca TO weaponry was cancelled? Did you ever hear that?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not hear that. I was informed that these arms were distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I have, in fact, served a document on the Defence this morning, Your Honours. Copies have been supplied for the use of Your Honours as well. I wonder if it could just be put to him simply in respect of the fact as to whether he would concede or not concede that point. So whether this is tendered subsequently in evidence, we will remain -- it is with Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked 340.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, you will see that document dated the 10th of May, 1992. I would really, sir, just draw your attention to paragraph 1 of the order. It says "is issued" and then paragraph 1. Now, sir, is it correct that that states that "the agreement between the HVO and the so-called Busovaca TO on the distribution of weapons is hereby terminated, and it has been decided that Busovaca HVO forces take over all weapons, equipment, material, as well as the barracks." That would appear to be correct; is that so, sir?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's what it says, that the reached agreement is terminated between the HVO and the so-called Busovaca TO, and it's to take over all the weapons, equipment, material, and the barracks by the Busovaca HVO from the TO. Yes. This document I am not familiar with. This is the first time that I see it. As a person who took part in some of the meetings, I have information that these weapons were distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, if I may move on, Mr. Alilovic, you say that, almost in due course, the Muslims set up a parallel, parallel kind of local government for themselves; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: One thing you haven't really mentioned, sir, is the impact of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna which was formed, was it not, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Is it not true, sir, that that Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna was, in fact, set up to be an independent Croat state within the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I never viewed it in that way, and I think that this is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you, sir, have -- you have knowledge of the policies and the philosophies behind the formation of that Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna? You were aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course, some of it is known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Isn't it true that many people espoused a form of Croat nationalism and set that up as a state, as a sovereign state with its own territory; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, this is not true. I didn't think about it in that way, and I don't think the Croatian people thought about it in that way. Why? Simply because in speaking about that, about the inertia of the Muslim side in the sense of what was happening to the Croatian people, that the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina had the need to create a kind of body which would be able to self-organise and do something, but this has nothing to do with a state or the creation of an entity that would be like a state. That's ridiculous. For me, that's ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you hear, sir, that, in fact, in Sarajevo in September of 1992, there was actually a Supreme Court decision declaring the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna to be an illegal state, as no state? Did you ever hear of that? You didn't hear of that?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't hear. I don't know how there could be a decision on the abolishment of a state when this was not a state. This was an economic, cultural, and territorial entity. This is how we interpreted it in the Croatian corps, and I personally took it to be this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So you are saying then at least we have an entity which is ethnically, socially, economically, and territoriality a Croat entity; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this was an entity where there was a considerable number, according to its structure, a considerable number of Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Is it not so that during the period particularly of 1992, the HVO, as an institution, made it clear that they would hold the power within that region?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am not aware that they would hold power in that region but that they would take the initiative in the sense of organising and preparation for defence. Wanting and attempting together with persistence and patience together with the Muslims to organise a defence against a common enemy. And I have to say this again, this was an activity that would go on up until the time of the conflict, and if we had objectively dealt more seriously with this problem, the conflict, the clash, would not have taken place in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, I would suggest to you, Mr. Alilovic, that the setting up of a parallel administration, or the committee for the protection of interests of the Muslims, was, in some measure, prompted by the controls being exerted by the HVO; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Which controls do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: General administrative and local government control in the area.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the control of the local administration, the Muslims participated as well, since they, in view of the fact that they did not want to participate in the authority which is called the Croatian Defence Council, they organised a parallel authority where they established their own control.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, do you recall a time when Dr. Mujezinovic and his colleagues actually submitted a complaint to your local government regarding materials to be used in schools, in education; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In which period? Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: This would have been in, I believe, mid 1992 because did the HVO not decree that certain materials would be used in schools mainly to remove any reference to the former Yugoslavia and, as it were, non-Croatian materials; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that, and I think that this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Sir, if I can move towards the end of 1992, and you said around the 20th of October, '92, there were clashes between the HVO and elements of the Bosnian Muslim forces at certain checkpoints; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that in the months subsequent to that, the tensions between the communities were very much greater?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question. Is it logical that there were tensions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: May I put it a different way, Mr. Alilovic? Is it true that subsequently, after October '92, there were numerous incidents of perhaps clashes between HVO and Muslim individuals, Muslim persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: In Vitez.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, in my testimony yesterday, I said that after that event, because of frequent meetings amongst the representatives of the political parties and representatives of both units, the situation was calmed down successfully. The extent to which it was tense after that, compared to the previous period, I couldn't really estimate that. I wasn't directly in the situation to assess that. But I think that the situation was calmed down successfully, thanks to agreements between the two sides and the implemented correct agreements regarding, for example, the division of arms within the factory and the attempt and further negotiations to attempt to establish a line of defence as long as possible against our common enemy. So I personally did not think that the situation after October 20th became significantly worse.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So, Mr. Alilovic, if I understand you correctly, you still personally view the position at that time as being one where the Muslims and Croats still had a common outside enemy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Absolutely. Yet, within something like four to five months of that time armed conflict broke out between Muslim and Croat. If I can move forward, sir, to the date of the 16th of April, 1993, I believe that you stated that you were at home and awakened to the sound of gunfire early in the morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I believe you said that you were summoned to try and go and see Mr. Santic, but you couldn't move until the next day, the 17th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So you -- sorry. I'm going too fast. So you stayed at home, did you, the whole of that day?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And presumably you were unable to see much of what went on in Vitez during that day?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course I wasn't able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: More particularly, sir, you clearly would not have any evidence to offer as to what happened in Ahmici village on that day?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You and your department were not involved in the checking and preparation of casualty figures for any of the victims of the actions of that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: If you offer an opinion as to any numbers, it is purely what you may have picked up in subsequent times from other parties?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had the opportunity to hear this at the meetings when we were talking about information. Then I had the opportunity to hear that at official meetings of the government. These were relevant facts, first of all, if I mentioned them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, sir, from the 16th of April events continued in Vitez. Did you become aware of such things as the rounding up of Muslim civilians and others?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Is it not true that a number of Muslims were detained in the cinema building and more in the Dubravica school? They were used as detention centres?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't consider them to be detention camps. They were temporarily placed there, these people. I know that this was in the cinema building because I had the opportunity to see that when I was going to work, and I could hear this information at a meeting of the HVO government, which we talked about earlier during the presentation of one of the documents signed by Mr. Santic, indicating his desire and his recommendations to release immediately a certain number of persons before any kind of agreement was reached on exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But you would concede, therefore, sir, that these numbers of Muslim persons were held in those locations and were not allowed to leave of their own will?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I will agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you hear subsequently about such things as detainees being taken to the lines to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You didn't hear that?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you hear of the transfer of Muslim detainees to the Kaonik camp where they were further detained?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you hear about searches and seizures in civilian apartments in Vitez during that period?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about that at an official meeting but this is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But on the other hand, did you hear of any form of detention facilities or rounding up of Croat civilians and people being detained in the Vitez area?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard more or less as much as there was this on the Croatian side in the regions which, during the first days of the conflict, that there were also similar things happening on the Muslim side, similar detentions. I heard this at the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Would this have been in Vitez, sir, in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the region of the Vitez municipality. This happened in Poculica, Preocica. I remember those names. In Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Do you have any idea of the -- sorry, I will repeat. Did you have any idea of the numbers involved in those particular locations?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: These were all the people who did not manage to escape, as far as I know, not -- I don't have a precise number, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have reached, in fact, a kind of subject matter break-point there and it may be convenient for you to order the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. We will take a 30-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, in the course of your evidence in chief you referred to a document being an HVO document relating to a contract to supply goods with the Sutra company run by Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic; is that correct? Or represented, I'm sorry, represented by Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't mention a contract.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: But rather an offer, a bid by Mr. Kupreskic, when we were preparing food supplies for the winter for the citizens of Vitez, that Mr. Kupreskic, or, rather, the company Sutra, was one of the bidders who offered to supply those goods at more favourable terms than others, and he was selected.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And so he was one of the selected contractors and was able then to conduct business selling goods; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You made mention of the fact that in the course of his work he entered both Muslim and Croat houses delivering things?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But to be absolutely clear, this was simply in the course of business for which he earned income for his company?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In this area, yes, that applies to all the contractors. That applies to all the contractors. I too was in the field throughout that period and afterwards. But it was also mentioned that Mr. Kupreskic carried out his activities throughout the period up to the conflict and even during the first days of the conflict, as far as conditions allowed, and immediately after the signing of the truce with the Muslims these activities were resumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, you were shown a form, a document, purporting to be a claim for reparations to a house, a house in the name of Mrs. Kupreskic, I believe, and in respect of lost or damaged goods. Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Do you recall the date of that document, or at least the year?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the report of the commission for the estimation of damages compiled after the truce with the Muslim Bosniak side. Such reports are being drawn up even today. This document was done after the truce. It may have been in '96 or'97. I do not recall the date exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, your department did not do any work in respect of the War Damage Commission; is that correct? It wasn't part of your duty?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Except with respect to the goods mentioned in the report when the total damages is summed up, so then it would affect that department. But as for the estimation of the damage on a building, that was not part of the work of my department.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And so would the work of your department, in that respect, be to verify prices and quantities if they're claimed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So you would not be in a position to know whether goods were taken or destroyed, but you could, if given a list of goods, you would have been able to price them for the commission and say, "Yes, that is the price." Is that a correct interpretation?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was in a position know that there were such appropriation of goods. And at the time we were not in a position to make all the proper calculations and everything else, but after the truce with the Muslims and the Bosniaks, through the defence ministry, those damages were checked, data collected and efforts were made to compensate the damages. So this too goes beyond the framework of my duties, except for checking the goods taken and pricing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I wonder if at this point, please, the registrar could kindly arrange for Prosecutor's Exhibit 329 to be handed to the witness? Will you please tell the Court, Mr. Alilovic, what does that document appear to be?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I'm able to understand, this is a certificate issued when collecting data, by the defence department, to confirm participation in units in order to acquire rights to shares. Time will show, regarding the agreement with the Muslim side regarding additional remuneration, a decision had to be taken, so that on both sides there were certain abuses with respect to the issuance of such certificates, the aim being to get a certificate for as long a period as possible to gain greater remuneration. I think this problem has still not been resolved regarding such additional remuneration. I too have a certificate of this kind, so that is how I interpret it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And in fact, does the certificate refer to the conscription of an individual, and is that individual Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic, son of Franjo, born the 1st of January, 1958; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This certificate is issued in the name of Mr. Kupreskic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And does it indicate that he was a member of the 92nd Viteska Homeguard Regiment from the 16th of April, 1993 to the 15th of January, 1996?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is evident from this certificate that he was assistant commander for health matters, although I didn't know that at the time, and that at first, at the beginning, I know that he drove an ambulance, and because of the condition of his health, because he has a heart problem, he was not recruited on a regular basis and he didn't do his military service in the former JAN because of that condition. That is probably why he was assigned to this post, assistant commander for health, although I wasn't aware of that. What I did see was him driving an ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So yesterday, sir, when you were asked by Defence counsel about whether Mr. Kupreskic was mobilised, you initially said you didn't really know, but later when asked the question, "He wasn't mobilised?" you said, "No." But in fact, you didn't know at the time, did you?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I always said that I didn't know, I think, and my reply now again is that I don't know. But you're asking me on the basis of this document what it means, and I think I have provided an answer as best I could since I too have a similar certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You have, sir, and I thank you for it. Mr. Alilovic, moving, if I may, to a couple of the documents we have seen this morning. You were shown -- this is D52/2, if the witness needs to look at it again --

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I saw this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: It is just to confirm -- clearly it would seem that Ivan Santic had considerable concerns about the detained Muslims in Vitez at that time, late April; you say that is correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't see Mr. Santic having concerns about the detained but, rather, I spoke to him to the effect that it would be good to be reasonable and to try and release a significant portion of those detained because for a number of reasons, this would be a good sign towards dealing with the situation that we were faced with at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So it seems the civilian HVO administration was trying to do something about the detained Muslims in Vitez, hence this document?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly. As I have explained, it would be a sign of goodwill, prompting the other side to act similarly, because on that occasion when we discussed this, I heard that several detainees in Poculica and Preocica had been killed, and then this would be an attempt towards carrying out an exchange. Anyway, he didn't believe it necessary to detain many of those people at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: If I could move on, sir? You saw another document, this is marked D51/2 -- perhaps we could have a brief look at that again? Mr. Alilovic, correct me if I misunderstand, but this announcement appears to me to show concern of the HVO civilian government in Vitez at what they perceive to have been crimes committed by participants in conflict in the area of Vitez at that time; would you say that is a fair interpretation by me?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: That would include, sir, perceived criminal activity by units of the HVO military as well as any allegations against other parties; is that so?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the time, we were aware of a large number of casualties and we were already informed at the time that crimes had been committed on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Indeed so. And one of the crimes that you feel you had in mind at that time was, in fact, the attack on the Ahmici village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The way in which it was done, it was already clear by then that this was a crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, and were you, in fact, even present at a large meeting held on the 29th of April, 1993? I believe the location may have been Citluk, unless I'm misinterpreting the word entirely. Perhaps I could further refresh your memory: It was hosted by Mr. Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Citluk?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: That might be the word for "date" because it's next to the date. I may be wrong. I don't understand the language well enough. Were you aware, sir, of this large meeting chaired by Mate Boban on the 29th of April of '93?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I remember perhaps that there was a meeting in '92 which I did not attend, but I remember, from the media, roughly at the time the HVO was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: But the 29th of April, '93, the conflicts were still ongoing and they were gaining in intensity, so I really have no recollection about that date in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Just referring there again. At around that time, were you aware of Mr. Ivica Santic attending any particularly large gathering or meeting with political leaders at that time?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In '93, you mean? In '93?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Yes, in '93.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I wonder if I might just have one moment to confer with my colleagues for just a second? I'm much obliged to Your Honours. I have just a couple more matters. I shall be very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: In respect of people mobilised into service with the HVO military, Mr. Alilovic, are you aware whether conscripts were actually paid? Were they paid rather like the people who signed contracts with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know something. The people who signed a contract with the HVO were paid something when it was possible to raise the necessary funds. As for those who were mobilised subsequently, I am not aware of anyone being paid anything except for a certain period, if some funds were available, then people were given some compensation. So this was on an ad hoc basis. I remember that on a number of occasions, some remuneration was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But there was no guarantee of a daily rate of pay for a conscripted soldier?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Well, that actually concludes my questions, Your Honours. I would like, please, to tender Exhibit P340 which I placed before the witness. That was the document bearing, amongst others, the signature of Dario Kordic. That concludes my cross-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. No objection? So P340 is admitted into evidence. We may now move on to re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can announce that the witness will be re-examined by Attorney Luko Susak and Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, the Prosecutor asked you about the existence of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean the formation of Herceg-Bosna and the existence. Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did it exist as a separate entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina? But let me ask you something else: Are you aware of the referendum on the integrity of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Was such a referendum carried out?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course I am familiar with it. It was held at the end of February 1992, I think. I think it was the 29th, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are you aware of the results of that referendum?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I am. The question at the referendum was answered by "Yes" I would say by the vast majority of the Muslim and Croat people. Unfortunately, not by the Serb people. But roughly 99 per cent of these first two peoples endorsed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said 99 per cent. You said this applies to both together. What about the Croats?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think roughly the same percentage of Croats voted in favour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So the referendum was on the wholeness of Bosnia-Herzegovina, its integrity. The Prosecutor asked you a question about the deterioration of relations between Muslims and Croats, so this prompts me to ask you: How did the HDZ, as a Croatian party, cooperate with the SDA party of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I have explained that at sufficient length on the first day of my testimony. The forms of cooperation were frequent meetings arranged whenever the need arose to coordinate views on particular issues or to try to influence a change of opinion, so that meetings of that kind were held frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were any conclusions passed at that level?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, conclusions and recommendations were passed at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When did that cooperation cease in that form?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, cooperation in that form did not cease until the outbreak of the conflict, and, in fact, it continued several days after the outbreak of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When did those forms of cooperation begin?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Immediately after the elections, and especially, as I said on the first day of my testimony, after the positions became evidently contradictory with regard to the aggression against the Republic of Croatia and the amassing of Serbian forces and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you give us the dates for this, roughly?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The preparations for the aggression on Croatia started, in fact, immediately after the elections. Actually, all the mass media and prominent international persons were forecasting the break-up of Yugoslavia and that this would not take place by peaceful means. This was something we could hear on the media on a daily basis. And since the approach to this issue varied in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and even in Vitez, views were divided, there was a need for the leading political parties to meet more frequently, to exchange views, to try to achieve a rapprochement of views and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But, Mr. Alilovic, could you give us a date, a rough date for this, the year, the month?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was particularly intensive at the end of August, September of 1991 already when significant positions were taken, differing positions, between the HDZ and the SDA regarding opposition to the return or the withdrawal of the JNA army from Slovenia and their redeployment in the area of Zenica, then the question of cessation of sending recruits to the JNA, then also expression of disagreement with the JNA's decision to place TO armaments under its control, then also the decision to see and establish what the TO had at its disposal at that time.
