This was the sort of thing over which meetings were held frequently between the two parties, and I think those meetings very often were successful. A meeting that I'm very familiar with in August 1991, it was stated that inter-ethnic relations were still good, but in view of the situation and the views adopted by the official authorities and by the SDA in Bosnia-Herzegovina, they could deteriorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, we will now move to another area. It will only be a short question. You spoke a lot yesterday and today about exchanges. You mentioned Dubravica and the cinema building. Do you know in which way did the Muslims leave Dubravica?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how they left, but I know that at a meeting at UNPROFOR, it was agreed to carry out an exchange and that, in this sense, it was carried out. How it was carried out, I don't know. I know, I had the opportunity later to hear that these people were released to their homes, but the exchange was not carried out as agreed at UNPROFOR. Excuse me. We were informed about this by Mr. Pero Skopljak, and I had the opportunity to hear this, that at a meeting at UNPROFOR, I don't remember exactly what date, he said -- he was taken out from the meeting or representatives of the civilian bodies were taken out from the meeting and then only representatives of the two military groups remained, military officials from the highest levels of the Zenica corps, so in this sense we were surprised to hear that the exchange was not carried out as agreed, and Mr. Pero Skopljak informed us on that occasion that he was not present at the time that this agreement was reached about the definite form of the exchange but that this was done by Mr. Mario Cerkez. So it was agreed for these people to be released. How they were released, how they left, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did you say the meeting was held at UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the UNPROFOR base at the elementary school in Stara Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who was at that meeting at the beginning? You said that Pero Skopljak informed you.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: At one of the meetings afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know who took part in those talks at the UNPROFOR base at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've already said that. I know that Mr. Pero Skopljak attended from our side, Mr. Mario Cerkez, and then from the other side, I know only that they were high representatives of the BH army who were present, including the top representatives, maybe the corps commander or some other official.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Susak. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, very briefly, you said, when you were talking about the permit for Kupreskic Vlatko, this is document 339, were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I considered myself as being mobilised by the fact that I was working there, but I didn't get an official piece of paper on this, that I was an official member of the HVO government, until later, so I didn't have an official document so that I could present, introduce myself in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you whether you were a representative of the HVO government but whether you got any kind of confirmation that you were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were you, in fact, mobilised as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not as a soldier, I was not mobilised as a soldier, but I do have a document that I was a participant in the war from the time that I started to work in the HVO government.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: From what date is this?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: My document bears the date from the end of June. I don't remember exactly. At the end of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What was the formal right that you enjoyed under such a document? What were your rights?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I understand, as far as I have been informed so far, I only had the right to additional salary, and this is a part that could be used later in order to purchase state-owned property or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this is, in fact, a right to have shares?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The right to an additional extra salary which can be in the form of shares which could be used for the purchase of some things, or for the payment of some obligations which will be regulated by the state later, but this has not been regulated yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It hasn't been regulated yet or nobody has actually exercised their rights arising from this document?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it hasn't been regulated, nor has anybody so far exercised any rights arising from this document, including myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this is a decision for people in accordance with their participation in the defence in some form or another, certain rights are granted; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So these documents that are issued for this purpose are issued retroactively; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. They were issued during the course of 1996, even '97, and as far as I know, this has not been completed, this process.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do these documents contain exact data or this data is changing in order to provide people with even greater rights as far as the shares are concerned?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it's confirmed that in the overall balance, in the overall available resources there were abuses from both sides. I mean, the HVO and the Muslim sides, abuses in the issuance of such documents, that perhaps somebody had been engaged earlier in orders that they could enjoy greater rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So my question to you is: Do these documents contain exact information, precise information that we can use?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I think not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Prosecution's document 340. The Prosecution has shown you this order and stated that under point 1 in the order it is stated that the agreement is terminated between the HVO and the Busovaca TO regarding the distribution of weapons.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I saw this point 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In the introduction it is stated that the reason that this order is issued is because of the brutal armed attacks by the forces of the so-called Busovaca TO led by Dervis Sarajalic against HVO forces on the road to Sendula's bridge against the barriers and with the purpose of implementing the decision by the Crisis Committee during conflicts at Kaonik during which Darko Vuleta and Stipe were killed on the approach to from Busovaca. Can you see from this document that the agreement between Busovaca TO and the HVO was terminated because of this armed incident between the HVO and the TO forces?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is evident.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And is it obvious that this was an armed attack by the TO against the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, this is probably a question of the violation of the agreement between the TO and the HVO agreement in a barracks. It's possible that this agreement was not observed and that for this reason the agreement was terminated, but I don't know this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, but you can see from this text that the termination occurred because of the incident. Do you know whether the agreement was terminated in its entirety or whether the agreement was perhaps observed about the division of arms between the HVO and the TO Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I stated my opinion that I had information that this task was carried out correctly, that it was done 50/50, and I even had the opportunity to discuss this with Mr. Mujezinovic, and I know from him, what he told me, that in certain parts on the lines they had some anti-aircraft guns and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So it's possible that the division of arms was carried out, according to your information?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is the information that I had. Whether this task was completed correctly I'm not sure, but for certain a part of the weapons from the Busovaca barracks were placed -- were given to the Muslim side as indicated by this conversation with Mr. Mujezinovic that I had in October '92 during a friendly meeting with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this refers to Busovaca, and you think that according to your information, the weapons may have been distributed. Regarding the agreement between the HVO and the TO in Vitez, were there any incidents there that would have led to the termination of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am not aware of any, that any incidents had taken place, and I think this was carried out to mutual satisfaction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you know that the weapons were divided between the TO and the HVO in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I know. Of course, not from -- based on documents and not from direct participation, but I do have such information. I don't have information indicating the opposite, not even from the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the number of detained Croats in Zenica in -- on April 16th and April 18th in '93?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the figure exactly, but I know that there was a large number of detained able-bodied Croats in Zenica in some notorious music school, and also in the prison in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And those people who were detained in the music school and the house of correction in Zenica, that they were not released even though an exchange was agreed on with the people from Zenica?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes. That is what I had been informed, that nobody was released from the house of correction in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: For the region of Poculica and Kruscica, Preocica, for those regions do you know when the Croats there were released and exchanged?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the precise date, but they were exchanged fairly quickly, and I think that this was within the overall exchanges that were carried out. I don't know precisely. I know that several people were killed in Poculica when they were detained on those premises, in those facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were there any detained Croats in Mahala?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Croats who lived in Mahala who were also detained by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, several families , maybe ten. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did these people -- were these people part of the exchange? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I remember when Sefer Halilovic came, and Petkovic, I don't know his name. There were attempts, in this sense, to carry out an exchange, and I think that an exchange was carried out to a certain extent, and that people were convinced that this will end quickly, so that people did not leave immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have one question for you, Mr. Alilovic. May I refer you to document D51/2? Did you say -- this is the announcement of the civil HVO government of Vitez on the extraordinary session 24th of April, 1993. Did you say that you took part in this extraordinary session, on the 24th of April, 1993, as a member of the civil HVO government?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I stated that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And did you take part in the drafting of this announcement?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not take part directly in the composition of the announcement, but I did participate directly at the meeting and I did take part in the discussion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: On the substance of this announcement. So you agreed that the announcement should be drafted?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention to point 3, item 3, where the command of the -- well, the civil HVO government of Vitez demanded from the commander of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia to carry out a detailed investigation of all individual cases of flagrant violations of International Humanitarian Law. I wonder whether you later became aware of any such investigation being carried out into alleged violations either by the BH army or by the HVO units.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you were not informed of any such investigations. You don't know the follow-up given to this announcement which was actually requested to the HVO government -- HVO operative command?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what happened further regarding this matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In particular, do you know whether any follow-up was given with regard to what you termed the crimes being committed in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean directly after this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know really. The conflict was escalating, unfortunately. I had a lot of work to do, and I don't know whether anything was done regarding this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I assume there is no objection to the witness being released? Mr. Alilovic, thank you so much for coming here to give evidence in court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Vlado Alilovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before we move on to our next witness, I wonder whether the Prosecutor could set out the various arguments that he announced this morning. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: (No translation)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what you just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I would be glad to do so, Mr. President. I was just saying that I would like to raise two matters having to do with the organisation of the proceedings, and which appear to me to require a rapid ruling by the Trial Chamber. The first of those questions has to do with the alibi defence provided by Vlado Santic, and the second has to do with the directive of the Trial Chamber, according to which the Prosecution must, several days before the cross-examination, submit to the Defence the exhibits that it intends to use. Regarding the first issue, the Defence of alibi by the accused Vlado Santic. We have received a document dated 16th January, 1999, that is Saturday, according to which we have been notified that implementing Article 67(A) of the Rules of procedure, that is the defence of alibi by the accused Vlado Santic, three witnesses have been named. Those witnesses will say that the accused Vlado Santic was in Vitez at the time of the acts attributed to him, that what appears from those documents, and it is finally specified that the accused will not testify himself. Mr. Pavkovic, who is the author of this document, tells us that it is not, strictly speaking, a new document, but, rather, a confirmation of a previous notification of December 1997, which, according to him, remains in effect. I wish to note and ask the Trial Chamber to note that a letter dated the 21st January, 1998, received by fax by the Office of the Prosecutor, the attorney of the accused Vlado Santic withdrew this defence of alibi by a letter which has no ambiguity in it. It is indicated in that letter that a new indictment was about to be drafted, and that according to that indictment the accused will specify his intention to abide by his defence of alibi or not, and in the last paragraph of that letter it says that the Office of the Prosecutor will be informed of the decision regarding the application of Rule 67. There is no point in my reminding the Trial Chamber the contents of Article 67 -- Rule 67. As all of us here present know, that requires notification prior to the beginning of the proceedings at the latest, and I think at the beginning of our proceedings we had a discussion on the defence of alibi. Your Trial Chamber made a ruling interpreting the Rules and specifying that a defence which would prove that one was not in Ahmici on the 16th of April, 1993 should be considered as defence of alibi in the sense of Rule 67. On that day, we had a debate, Mr. Pavkovic was present, and this did not provoke any reaction from him. Five months after the beginning of this trial we received this notification regarding application of Rule 67. In view of the present situation, I have two comments to make. The first would be that the Prosecution wishes the Rules to be implemented and in the -- under the conditions envisaged. The accused did not notify us of the alibi defence within the fixed time period. The Prosecution would not like an error to compromise the means of defence of the accused. I think that would be contrary to the general principles of law as I understand them, that the accused be prevented to prove that he was not in Ahmici on the day of the crimes he's charged with, and that his freedom of action in this court should be limited in any way. In view of that, the Prosecution refers to Article 20 of the Statute, and that is requiring, at the same time, respect of the Rules , but also respect of the rights of the Defence and a fair and equitable trial, and we would propose a flexible interpretation of the Rules which would satisfy these three imperatives, respect of the Rules, respect of the rights of the Defence and a fair trial. What would that mean? That would mean that the three witnesses who have been named in this document of the 16th of January, 1999, could be heard first by -- interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor before their appearance in court, and secondly, they would be admitted into the proceedings on the basis of this defence of alibi. I underline that we are not reiterating a previous document of December 1997, in which six witness were is cited, whereas in January 1999 only three witnesses have been cited, two of whose names have already appeared and the third being a new name, at least a new name in these proceedings. The witnesses could be heard by your Trial Chamber, and it would be admissible for them to support the alibi of Vlado Santic, but we would also say that the accused Vlado Santic must testify in accordance with Rule 67(B) in application of this defence of alibi. That would be a flexible interpretation of the Rules that I have referred to, and unless the accused decides otherwise, the Defence would question the accused on the alibi as well as the Prosecution on the same issue except if Defence counsel decide otherwise. In that way, the accused would testify about his own alibi. We would be respecting, if not the letter, then at least the spirit of the Rules, and the right of the Defence and the accused of Vlado Santic would be fully observed and the imperative of a fair process and an equality of arms of the two armies would be ensured. That would be my first point. My second point is the following: It has to do with your directive issued last Friday according to which the Prosecutor must, several days in advance, communicate to the Defence the documents it intends to use in its cross-examination. This directive causes great difficulty for us which I would like to refer to briefly. Today, we are in the following situation: A procedural decision having to do with the procedure was taken on Friday. Yesterday, five of the Defence attorneys submitted an appeal. Your Trial Chamber, by majority decision, decided that we proceed with the proceedings and that we should agree to the requests of the Defence. I must say that we accept your ruling, and we fully understand the spirit behind it, and we understand and support the imperative of fairness; and if the Appeals Chamber admits the appeal of the attorneys, we could find ourselves in a very difficult situation. We do understand your decision. We just wish to ask that the appeal be dealt with with the greatest possible expediency, but we are aware that this may be difficult for various reasons. However, in view of the situation we find ourselves in now and regarding the future of these proceedings, until the Appeals Chamber makes a ruling in any event, all the attorneys who have called a witness may, at least regarding the first count, may examine the witness and also re-examine after the cross-examination by the Prosecution, and in view of this decision, we would ask the Trial Chamber to reconsider its directive, which is a cause of difficulty for us, from the point of view of law and from the point of view of fact. In law -- your Trial Chamber is fully aware of this but I wish to underline it -- that in law, we have no obligation to communicate in advance to the Defence the documents that we intend to use as evidence. Rule 66 of the Rules envisages only that at the request of the Defence, we should disclose or, rather, give access to the Defence to those documents; and, on the other hand, the Prosecution must have access to the documents which the Defence intends to use. On the other hand, and still within the legal framework, in the interests of preserving the continuation of proceedings, if a document is submitted that it is not aware of and we know that a document may always be prompted by another testimony, so that again the rights of the Defence are fully respected and especially in the stage of the proceedings we are in now. From the standpoint of fact, the decision of the Trial Chamber is difficult to implement strictly by the Prosecution; in certain circumstances, it can constrain the activities of the Prosecution, and even if the decision is applied flexibly, which I understand the position of the Tribunal to be, it can cause incidents and endless discussions. Why is this instruction difficult to implement? Because a cross-examination is prepared not many days in advance, as you know, but it is prepared in the course of the examination-in-chief, and it is then when documents are selected that may be used for the cross-examination; and it is above all true that in the situation we are in and in view of the fact that we have very little information about the witnesses that are being called by the Defence, we have very little information of their status, their competencies, their fields of work and, above all, very little information of what the substance of their testimony will be. We had two examples. The first witness, Mr. Cilic, elaborated in great detail what was referred to in his summary. As for the second witness, Mr. Alilovic, the areas that he touched upon in the course of the examination-in-chief were very many, and we did not expect them to be the subject of his testimony. Just one example. He stated that he knew closely or personally two of the accused and referred to the professional activities of one of the accused, and this is an area of testimony which affects the first count of the indictment, and clearly our questions and our documents that we will use cannot be identified until we hear the examination-in-chief, and we also respectfully ask the Trial Chamber to reconsider its instructions -- the Appeals Chamber may take a different position regarding the organisation of the proceedings -- but bearing in mind the position taken by the attorneys of the Defence and their right to re-examine, so we are back in the situation that we had prior to those instructions. Those are all the remarks I wanted to make today, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Terrier. I suggest that we deal with these two matters separately. They are very important. First, there is the question having to do with the defence of alibi and which affects Mr. Pavkovic, so we are going to deal with that, and then there is another question that affects all the attorneys. I suggest that before we proceed to ask you for a point of clarification, Mr. Terrier, after that I will ask Mr. Pavkovic to take a position on the questions that have just been raised by Mr. Terrier. As for the second point, I would suggest that after the break, one of the Defence attorneys can summarise, on behalf of all the attorneys, the position of the Defence on the position of the Prosecution regarding the documents or the exhibits that the Prosecution has been asked to disclose to the Defence in advance. Mr. Terrier, let me ask you: If I understood you well, you suggested that regarding the three witnesses that are going to be called by Mr. Pavkovic, that they should be interviewed by you, by the Prosecution first, in private or in the presence of counsel, Mr. Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I will be guided by your ruling. Those witnesses may be in Bosnia and it may be difficult. We would like to interview them, not on the eve of their testimony, we would like to hear them several days in advance so that we can do the verification. If such a decision is taken, we would contact those witnesses. Of course, if the witnesses refuse, we have no way of forcing them, but if they accept, we would meet them wherever they are, which means probably in Bosnia, I don't have the specifics, and then we can proceed to verify, to make the necessary verifications, and then we can proceed with the defence of alibi here before your Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But you would be ready to agree that the interview be held in the presence of the attorneys of the three witnesses, Mr. Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: A representative of the Defence, yes, and a reservation that that should not be an impediment to that interview so that it can be done quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Another question before giving the floor to Mr. Pavkovic. Mr. Terrier, how much time would you need to interview the three witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, you mean ahead of their appearance in court? I think a month, a month and a half would be desirable. I think it should be done as soon as possible because of the necessary verification later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So let me correct what I just said. The question that I addressed to you regarding the presence of an attorney, it would be better to envisage the presence of an investigator named by the Defence rather than the attorney himself. Having said that, my question is addressed to Mr. Pavkovic to see what his reaction is to the proposal just made by the Prosecution regarding the defence of alibi.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I listened very carefully to the arguments of the Prosecution, and in brief, because it is already time for a break, I would like to say the following: If I understood it correctly, the Prosecutor supports the view that the Defence cannot refer to the regulations of Rule 67(A), but this would really be the application of Rule 67(B). First of all, I would like to point out that I support the stand of the Prosecution as far as the application of Article 21 of the Statute of this Tribunal is concerned. The Defence of Vlado Santic, in the motion of the 16th of this month that was mentioned by the Prosecution, briefly explained its position, keeping in mind, first of all, the decision of this Court of the 11th of January under point 5. We submitted the required supporting documents with this motion with which we confirm what we cite in the motion. What we submitted, for understandable reasons, was not known to the Court before and it was not known to the Court particularly before the ruling of the 11th of January of 1999, of this year, so that is why we submitted these documents. I would like to make two key points. The first, when we are talking about the motion by the Defence of January 21st of 1998, which was also referred to by the Prosecution, for which he requires additional explanations, and I state now, which is contrary to what the Prosecutor has stated, and that is that the Defence of Vlado Santic never withdrew its information from December of 1997 that Vlado Santic intends to defend himself by alibi. In this document of the 21st of January of 1998, it states that the Defence does not insist on the alibi. Permit me to clarify what this means. I would like to remind you that the time then was when the amended indictment was announced and in view of the fact that the Defence by alibi related to the indictment prior to that, out of caution we then stated that we do not insist. When the amended indictment was issued, it became obvious that the accusations that we intended to defend ourselves from by alibi had been unchanged; therefore, in the amended indictment, the same count numbers were kept so that the incriminating points for Vlado Santic were cited in points 16 -- Counts 16 to 19, so this is where our intention to defend from alibi still stand. The second key point that I would like to state before this Tribunal is the knowledge of the Defence or the fact that the Defence has found out about an important witness, Mr. Slavko Marin, who testified in the Blaskic case. His testimony was given after these proceedings started, after the 17th of August of last year. His testimony is very important regarding the defence by alibi, so we were not in a position, according with Rule 67(A)(ii), to find out about this matter before proceedings started, and we were not able to inform the Prosecutor. In conclusion, I would like to state the following: In our motion of the 16th of January, 1999, we repeated and did not state for the first time, for the reasons that I have stated, and we have proposed these witnesses. I agree at this moment for the Prosecution to meet with the witnesses and talk with them in my presence, but permit me to consult the accused before that and to see if the witnesses are able to comply with this request. Your Honours, these would be the reasons that need to be kept in mind when ruling on this matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Pavkovic. However, Counsel Pavkovic, with all due respect, let me put the record straight. It is very clear from your fax of the 21st of January, '98, to the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Mark Harmon, that, (1), you said: "As the new indictment is about to be raised, the aforesaid decision of the accused's intention to defend himself by the existence of alibi is now not valid." Point 1. Point 2. You said, "You will be" -- "you," the Prosecution -- "will be informed about his decision pursuant to sub-Rule 67(A)(ii)." So it is very clear, therefore, that you are under Rule 5, noncompliance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. You have simply not complied with Rule 67, and so therefore, I think it is only fair for the Prosecution to propose a suggestion which does take into account the rights of the Defence. But it is clear -- and this is the assumption of the Court -- that you have not complied with Rule 67(A), and this is very clear from the very wording of your letter, fax sent on the 21st of January, 1998. In light of all this, I would welcome, as soon as possible, your stating a position on the proposal of the Prosecutor, first of all, that the three witnesses be interviewed in the presence of one of your investigators a few weeks or at least a month before they are called here and about the position of the accused; namely, the request of the Prosecution that the accused should testify, of course, only on the question of alibi, as Mr. Terrier pointed out quite clearly. This being so, let us now wait for your further comments on this matter and then we will make a ruling. I propose that we now break for 15 minutes, and when we reconvene, I hope that one of the Defence counsel will state the common position, if any, of the various Defence counsel on the second issue raised by Mr. Terrier, namely, whether or not this Court should stick to the ruling we made concerning the passing of documents to Defence counsel prior to cross-examination of witnesses. As I said, before making a ruling, we would like to have your comments. So we are adjourned now for 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Shall we deal with the matter we left in abeyance before reconvening so that we settle this matter before the new witness is brought in? I wonder whether any Defence counsel is prepared to state the views of the Defence counsel on the second issue raised by the Prosecutor. All right. If not, we will make a ruling on this matter. Counsel Pavkovic, do you want to clarify your condition with respect to the alibi question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours permit me, I would like to add to what I've already said. I must say once again, of course I will see later if your ruling on the fact that the accused must testify and he decides not to testify, whether I will accept such a decision, because this is the only reason why I believe that this defence would not be acceptable for the defence of Vlado Santic, but the person who wrote the motion of -- when you see the entire motion, especially the first sentence, when you keep in mind what was happening at the time, that this was a new indictment, we did not insist -- we never gave up. This, according to me, is the substance of the matter. So this is not the first time that I have stated the intention of the accused to defend himself by alibi; I did that before. I do not have any other explanation Your Honours. I think that the whole motion, the spirit of the motion should be interpreted in this way, because that was my intention. I allow that it was -- this position was not precisely defined later, but this notification was never withdrawn about the defence of alibi from December of 1997. Thank you. I don't want to take up any more of your time, but this is the substance of my position, and I think in that instance, Rule 67(A)(ii) should be applied. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We may move on then to our next witness, and I understand from my documents that the next witness, who is a protected witness, has been called by counsel for Zoran Kupreskic and Mirjan Kupreskic only. No? Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is precisely the confusion that I was talking about. Joint witnesses are on this list, and this witness is on a separate list of Mr. Puliselic, and Mr. Puliselic has called this witness. So he is the one -- so this is a witness of Defence Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Only Counsel Puliselic has called the next witness. Thank you. All right. So we can bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could be allowed, this witness I propose protective measures because of a specific situation in accordance with Rule 79. I propose a closed session throughout the testimony in order to protect the identity of this witness and also for other reasons, namely the witness would like -- requests a closed session. The witness works on matters -- duties of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The registrar has rightly suggested that even when you are explaining the reasons for justifying protective measures we should be in closed session. So we will now go into a closed session and you can very briefly state the reasons for the protective measures and we will grant them. (Closed session).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: at 1.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday 24, the 21st day of January, 1999, at 9.00 a.m.
